spoken: On an Xbox controller the four face buttons are the coloured ones on the right side of the front. A is the green one at the bottom and confirms or selects. question: how do I change the batteries on this
spoken: Flip the controller face down so the back is up. Near the middle of the back, there's a battery cover. Slide it toward the bottom edge, then lift it off. Take out the two AA batteries, and put in two fresh ones with their ends matching the markings inside the bay. Put the cover back on by sliding it into place until it clicks. Don't mix old and new batteries together.

spoken: That red wire is a power feed for the convection fan. It is crimped to a spade terminal on the fan motor coil and runs up to the control panel, where it links into the switches that run the fan. In this photo, a red wire arcs across the middle of the motor housing, and its far end goes toward the knob panel. Before you touch it, unplug the oven and let any stored charge drain. question: how does the fan motor in this work
spoken: This is a small AC motor, usually a shaded-pole type on a little oven fan like this. When it gets power, the coil creates a magnetic field that keeps pushing the rotor around, and the rotor spins the fan blade. That blade circulates hot air past the heating elements so the food cooks more evenly. The motor only runs when the oven's switch sends power to it, and it's controlled from the front panel.

question: how do I replace the blade on this trimmer
spoken: Before you start, make sure the trimmer is switched off and the blade is handled carefully, since the edges are sharp. Then look at the square recessed area at the top of the handle, where the blade attaches. Hold the handle firmly and pull the old blade straight off the top, without twisting. To fit the new one, line it up with that same top area and press it down until it clicks into place. Give it a gentle tug to confirm it's locked before you use it.
